subject: math

objective.text: Sort and record data into a table using up to four categories. Use category counts to solve word problems.

source_ref.section: Lesson objective

explanations.title: Categories
explanations.text: A category is a group. We sort things into categories by their characteristics. A fish has scales and fins. A bird has feathers and wings.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (sort animals by characteristics)

explanations.title: A table organizes data
explanations.text: Data is information. A table puts data in rows. It is easier to count how many are in each category.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (organize our information, or data)

explanations.title: Tally marks
explanations.text: Make one tally mark for each thing. Count the marks to get the total. Then write the total as a number.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (record category counts using tally marks)

explanations.title: Tallies or numbers
explanations.text: Numbers give the total at once. Tally marks show the length of each group, so most and least are easy to see.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (which recording is easier to read)

explanations.title: Table direction
explanations.text: A table can go across or up and down. The data inside does not change.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (the orientation of the table)

explanations.title: How many more or fewer
explanations.text: To find how many more, compare two groups. Take away the same amount from both, or count the extra. A tape diagram can show it.

source_ref.section: Application Problem; Concept Development

examples.title: Sort animals
examples.text: Sort animals as bird, mammal, reptile or fish. Make tally marks in each row. Then write each total as a number.

source_ref.section: Concept Development

examples.title: Sort by habitat
examples.text: Sort the same animals by where they live: arctic, woodland or ocean. Record each count as a number.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (Chart 4)

examples.title: Penguins and whales
examples.text: 24 penguins and 18 whales. Compare the two. 24 minus 18 equals 6. There are 6 more penguins.

visual_generation_rules: Diffusion cannot count reliably. Any picture where an exact number of objects matters must be built by code (SVG or widget) or drawn by an artist.
Diffusion is allowed only for: style or background art, and single icons (one ball, one pencil, one leaf, one character) that code then tiles to the exact count.
Every visual must be checked by a person: the count shown must equal the stimulus in the question and the rubric answer key.
Animations are described as frames with exact counts per frame, so they can be built or generated and then checked frame by frame.
Visual explanations are valid only when the asset exists (pipeline doc, Planner rules).
